name: the-hover-url-card-has-no-ring-outside-its-border
description:
Reported with a screenshot: a hard light outline sits just outside the hover URL card's rounded border, which no other overlay surface has. The outline is the accent ring toast-stack.css gives every .toast - a status line sets no --ctc of its own, so the ring fell back to --ov-accent.

--ct-ring is not only paint. toast-surface.js reads it off the .toasts box and reports it as the third argument of toastStackSized, where atrium_toast_overlay_widget.mm stores it as stack_outset_ and offsets the widget by it. So the outset has to go with the ring, or the card gains a stray gap at the pane corner.

WHERE THE PIXELS ARE. The hover card hangs off the window's bottom leading corner over a flat light page. The card's own screen rect is recorded below from the /toast widget's window origin, so the probe coordinates under it can be read against a number rather than guessed.

actions.note: past the show debounce the hover path keeps

actions.expression: (() => { const a = document.createElement('a'); a.href = 'https://short.example/a'; a.textContent = ''; a.style.cssText = 'position:fixed;left:0;top:0;width:100%;height:100%;z-index:99;background:#000'; document.body.appendChild(a); return 'armed'; })()
actions.note: an opaque BLACK link over the whole web card. The ring is the accent at 45% over whatever is behind it, so a dark surround is what makes a light rim a large reading rather than a few counts on white.
REAL pointer move into the link

actions.expression: (() => { const t = document.querySelector('.toasts .toast .ctl'); return t ? t.textContent : 'no card'; })()
actions.note: THE CONTROL: every reading below is of this card, so a run that raised none must not satisfy them by measuring bare page

actions.expression: (() => { const c = document.querySelector('.toasts .toast'); if (!c) { return 'no card'; } return getComputedStyle(c).boxShadow; })()
actions.note: In the layout engine: the ring was a box-shadow, so none here means nothing paints outside the border box

actions.expression: (() => { const c = document.querySelector('.toasts .toast'); if (!c) { return 'no card'; } return getComputedStyle(c).borderColor; })()
actions.note: .ov-card gives every card a 1px border. The status-line rule sets border-color:transparent so the rim is invisible.

actions.expression: (() => { const c = document.querySelector('.toasts .toast'); if (!c) { return 'no card'; } return String(!!c.querySelector('.cti')); })()
actions.note: THE CONTROL for the rule's own selector: the new rule keys on :not(:has(.cti)), so a card that turned out to carry an icon would be exempt and the reading above would mean nothing

actions.expression: (() => { const box = document.querySelector('.toasts'); if (!box) { return 'no stack'; } return getComputedStyle(box).getPropertyValue('--ct-ring').trim(); })()
actions.note: This is the value toast-surface.js sends as toastStackSized's third argument and the widget offsets itself by. 1px with no ring painted is the stray gap at the corner.

actions.expression: (() => { const c = document.querySelector('.toasts .toast'); if (!c) { return 'no card'; } const r = c.getBoundingClientRect(); return String(Math.round(r.top * 100) / 100); })()
actions.note: The top edge the stack anchors to. .toastroot .toasts sets top to var(--ct-ring), so this was 1 while the ring was reserved and is 0 with it gone.

actions.expression: (() => { const c = document.querySelector('.toasts .toast'); if (!c) { return 'no card'; } const r = c.getBoundingClientRect(); const w = document.documentElement.clientWidth; const h = document.documentElement.clientHeight; const r2 = (n) => Math.round(n * 100) / 100; return [r2(r.left), r2(w - r.right), r2(r.top), r2(h - r.bottom)].join(' '); })()
actions.note: EVIDENCE, ungraded: all four gaps. The leading one is not zero - toast-surface.js sizes the widget to the width it fitted the label to, not to the card's measured box, which this scenario does not grade.

actions.expression: (() => { const c = document.querySelector('.toasts .toast'); if (!c) { return 'no card'; } const r = c.getBoundingClientRect(); const R = (n) => Math.round(n); return [R(window.screenX + r.left), R(window.screenY + r.top), R(r.width), R(r.height)].join(' '); })()
actions.note: EVIDENCE, ungraded: the card's rect in screen pixels, which is where the region_mean probes below were placed from
the first stream in a run can deliver no frames

assertions.desc: THE CONTROL: the hover raised a card, so every reading below is of a real card
THE CONTROL: the hover card carries no icon, so the new :not(:has(.cti)) rule does apply to it
The .ov-card border is transparent on a status strip
The outset went with the ring, so the widget is not padded for paint nobody makes
The stack's top edge is flush in its widget, so nothing is reserved for a ring nobody paints

assertions.label: the-surround-is-dark
assertions.desc: THE CONTROL for the rim reading: bare page level with the card and clear of it. Without it a frame that lost the black link would let the miss below pass on a light page where a light rim cannot be told from its surround.

assertions.label: there-is-a-card-to-read
assertions.desc: THE CONTROL: the card's own paper, --ov-paper at 249,240,241. The card's screen position varies by a few pixels between runs, so this probe sits inside the card's vertical center rather than at its top edge.

assertions.label: the-row-above-the-border-is-page-not-rim
assertions.desc: This row sits well above the card's top edge (card starts around y=658-662 depending on the run). The old accent ring at 45% over black read about 46 across a 4px band above the card. The page reads near 0.
